prompt: Please generate an image. Locked painterly style: hand-painted stylized game art, chunky readable shapes, detail painted not modelled, mid-level detail, softer muted colours with gentle saturation, epic and luminous, never grim. The palette's warm gold and cool teal are painted into the surfaces, but the light is flat, even studio light: no strong key light, no cast shadows, no rim light. Use the attached images only as reference as described: the first attachment is always the style reference for palette and brushwork; later attachments are the approved designs to keep. Game-asset reference sheet for 3D modelling, wide landscape 16:9. Plain light neutral grey background, no scene, no sky, no clouds, no floating rock, no ground plane, a soft contact shadow only. Every piece fully isolated with clear space around it, nothing overlapping, nothing touching the edge, arranged in tidy rows, each with a small neat hand-lettered label underneath. GEAR AND PROPS sheet: Redraw of the attached reference sheet to the current spec: keep the same items and names. For this materials kit a new layout replaces the old one: four rows, one per tier, top to bottom, each row with its tier label at the left; every row has four columns, left to right: the resource node as found in the world, the raw piece, the refined piece, and one flat-on square seamless texture swatch (orthographic, no perspective). The four tiers are the same meshes with a different colour and trim mask, so draw the node, the raw piece and the refined piece with matching shapes in every row, changing only colour, surface and glow. Keep the same tiers and look as the attached sheet. Row 1 "Tier 1 Meadow birch": "Meadow birch tree", a pale straight birch with papery white bark and a few big leaf clumps; "Birch log", a cut log section with papery white bark; "Birch plank", a thick pale plank; "Birch texture". Row 2 "Tier 2 Rootwood": "Fallen root", a length of dense, dark, twisting fallen root timber with moss in its grooves (rootwood is cut only from roots that have already fallen); "Rootwood log", the same log shape as row 1 in dark twisting polished root timber; "Rootwood plank"; "Rootwood texture". Row 3 "Tier 3 Duskcrown yew": "Duskcrown yew tree", the same tree shape as row 1 as a dark evergreen yew with needle clumps; "Yew log", dark red-brown; "Yew plank", dark red-brown with a tight wavy grain; "Yew texture". Row 4 "Tier 4 Grudgeheart": "Fallen ancient limb", the same shape as the row 2 fallen root as a massive fallen limb of an ancient tree, moss and flowers over its bark, its cut face showing golden growth rings that glow faintly green; "Grudgeheart log", cut face with faintly glowing golden-green rings; "Grudgeheart plank"; "Grudgeheart texture". No crafted items, no extra pieces. Trees and fallen limbs are drawn reduced to fit the row; every label carries the real size only where the attached sheet or these words give it, and the scale figure stands beside the rows. Each item alone in three-quarter front view, in rows by family or tier, with thick chunky proportions: thick blades, solid rope, chunky grips, no thin parts. A plain neutral 1.8 m human silhouette labelled "1.8 m" stands on the sheet for scale, with everything at true scale to it. Title at the top: "Materials kit: woods".
